title: Bias–Variance Tradeoff — Bent Sight or Shaky Hand
key_insight: Bias is a consistent miss because the model is too limited. Variance is instability because the model follows small details of its training sample.
body:
## Bent Sight or Shaky Hand

One archer lands every arrow left of the target; another scatters arrows everywhere. Both are inaccurate for different reasons.

Bias is a consistent miss because the model is too limited. Variance is instability because the model follows small details of its training sample.

A useful model captures the lasting pattern without chasing every accident. Validation shows which problem is dominating.
common_mistakes: Choosing a remedy without comparing training and validation behavior.
Assuming model size alone determines effective complexity.
mini_exercise: Draw the situation from “Bent Sight or Shaky Hand” with three labeled steps, then explain what changes at each step.
real_world_usage: The tradeoff explains underfitting, overfitting, and why model complexity needs validation.
explain_back_prompt: Using the “Bent Sight or Shaky Hand” story, explain Bias–Variance Tradeoff without assuming the listener knows machine learning.
